Treasury Model for Tokenized Real-World Asset Liquidity

A treasury-driven protocol on BNB Chain that connects protocol-owned treasury management, productive capital deployment, collateralized credit and tokenized debt into one capital framework. The treasury acts as a yield and liquidity engine for tokenized real-world assets. Operations are funded from what the framework earns rather than from token emissions.

Treasury focus

Liquidity for tokenized real-world assets

As RWAs migrate onchain, token issuance alone does not produce functional markets. Institutional participants need reliable two-sided liquidity to enter, exit and rebalance without material market impact. The treasury supplies that inventory and market depth in eligible tokenized markets, and reinvests surplus to expand liquidity for the broader RWA ecosystem.

01
Revenue

Three streams

Transaction fees from liquidity provision on tokenized equities, ETFs and RWAs paired with stablecoins; yield from income-bearing RWAs; and appreciation on inventory held as markets recover.

02
Deployment

Valuation-aware entry

Capital is deployed only after material corrections, through staged tranches that improve the blended cost basis while the position continues to provide liquidity and generate fees.

03
Risk

No leverage

The model does not use perpetual futures or margin. Liquidation risk is eliminated. Controls include cash reserves, concentration limits and thesis-based stopping rules.

Operating model

A balance sheet designed to fund protocol operations

Seed proceeds form a protocol-owned treasury. Capital is deployed under an allocation and risk framework, with realized income intended to fund operations, reserves and ONMX holder value capture within the fixed token supply.

01
Form

Form the treasury

Token sales fund the treasury, whether seed, presale or public sale. The $3.5M seed round sets the initial treasury base, held under Safe multi-signature control.

02
Deploy

Deploy capital

Treasury capital is put to work in productive onchain positions: supplying liquidity to eligible markets to earn trading fees, holding assets positioned for appreciation, and, as the credit layer comes online, lending against collateral. A liquid reserve is held back at all times.

03
Allocate

Allocate surplus

Surplus after operating costs goes back into the treasury so it keeps growing. Part of it can fund airdrops that pay holders in stablecoins from treasury earnings, or ONMX buybacks once the token trades.
